title: Generate Your First SSH Key
description: No SSH key exists on this box; generate an ed25519 keypair with correct permissions.
scenario: You are about to be added to the jump-host rotation, and the policy requires key-based authentication with a modern algorithm: ed25519, no passphrase (the team's key agent handles unlocking), stored at the default location. Today ~/.ssh does not even exist. Generate the keypair and set the permissions SSH expects.
symptoms: `ls ~/.ssh` reports the directory does not exist
The jump-host onboarding checklist requires an ed25519 keypair
SSH refuses private keys whose permissions are too open
mission: Generate an ed25519 keypair at ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 (no passphrase), with the private key at mode 600, the directory at 700.

hints.title: The algorithm
hints.content: `-t ed25519` picks the modern Ed25519 algorithm — short keys, fast, and the current best practice over RSA.

hints.title: No passphrase this time
hints.content: `-N ""` supplies an empty passphrase; the two quotes are required so ssh-keygen does not prompt.

hints.title: Permissions are policy
hints.content: SSH enforces them: ~/.ssh at 700, private key at 600. Group/world-readable private keys get refused with 'UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE'.
